title: Granularity from bentness
statement: Let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional cube over $ bf_2$ to $ bf_2$. If the real sign encoding of $f$ is bent, meaning that every vector Fourier coefficient has absolute value $2^{-\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, then the function that takes value $1$ where $f=1$ and $0$ elsewhere is vector Fourier granular with granularity $2^{-(\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1)}$: each of its Fourier coefficients on the sign cube is an integer multiple of this number.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the $n$-dimensional $ bf_2$ cube to $ bf_2$
